annotations.description: 1.02 checkpoint(s) failed in the last 10 minutes.

diagnosis.summary: The Flink taskmanager was forcibly terminated (TaskExecutor shutdown, exit code 255) ~2 minutes ago, causing ~2 in-flight checkpoints to fail and triggering the alert. The job restarted automatically from its last checkpoint and is now RUNNING/STABLE, completing ~25 checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. Chaos Mesh is active and its pattern of repeated deployments correlates with pod terminations.
diagnosis.root_cause: A Flink taskmanager pod (`events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2`) was killed (exit_code 255, reason Unknown) approximately 1.9 minutes ago, causing the in-flight Flink checkpoints to fail. The Flink operator detected the failure, restarted the taskmanager (restarts_last_15m: 1.018), and the job resumed from its latest successful checkpoint. The job is now RUNNING/STABLE (uptime 96s at time of check) with 24.995 completed checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. Chaos Mesh (`chaos-mesh-local`) is installed and was updated several times recently; its deployment ~144 minutes ago aligns with an earlier round of pod terminations (exit_code 255 at ~140.9 minutes ago for all Kafka brokers and the Flink jobmanager), and subsequent chaos-mesh updates at ~94, ~44, ~31, and ~27 minutes ago suggest ongoing fault-injection experiments as the most likely cause of the taskmanager kill.
diagnosis.impact: Approximately 2 checkpoints failed during the 1–2 minute job restart window. Exactly-once delivery was preserved via the last good checkpoint. Consumer lag is 650 messages (expected catch-up after restart). No data was lost. Kafka is fully healthy (0 under-replicated, 0 offline partitions). Impact is limited to a brief processing delay.

evidence.finding: Job RUNNING/STABLE, uptime only 96 seconds, restarts_last_15m=1.018, failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104, completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995, consumer_lag=650. Taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 age_minutes=1.9. Jobmanager last_termination exit_code=255 reason=Unknown 140.9 minutes ago.
Warning/JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 minutes ago: 'The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — confirms the taskmanager was killed just before the checkpoint failures.

All 3 brokers Running/Ready, under_replicated_partitions=0, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0. Brokers also had exit_code=255 terminations ~140.9 minutes ago (aligns with chaos-mesh revision 9187ff9e9e6f deployed ~144.6 minutes ago).
chaos-mesh-local was deployed/updated at ~144.6, ~94, ~44, ~31, and ~27 minutes ago. The ~144.6 min deployment closely precedes the ~140.9 min pod terminations. No streaming pipeline app changes.
All 4 nodes (control-plane + 3 workers across zone-a/b/c) are Ready with no pressure conditions or cordons. Node failure is not the cause.
All ArgoCD apps Synced/Healthy including chaos-mesh-local (revision 2.8.5,47886843e767). No gitops sync failures.
Runbook docs/runbooks/pipeline.md#flinkcheckpointfailures states: a single failure during a broker restart or node drain is expected; job tolerates 3 consecutive failures before restarting.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job has already self-recovered: it is RUNNING/STABLE and completing checkpoints at the expected 10-second interval (~25 in the last 5 minutes). No manual restart is needed. The alert should clear as the failed_checkpoints_last_10m counter ages out of the window.

follow_ups: Confirm whether the Chaos Mesh fault injection experiment that killed the taskmanager was intentional. If so, consider raising the checkpoint failure alert threshold or silencing it during planned chaos runs.
Monitor consumer lag (currently 650) over the next 5–10 minutes to confirm the job is catching up at normal throughput.

Investigate the iceberg-exporter readiness probe failure (Warning/Unhealthy on Pod/iceberg-exporter-57567747cd-czzt2, 27 minutes ago) as a separate issue — it may affect Iceberg table health visibility.
Review the pattern of exit_code=255/Unknown terminations across Kafka brokers and Flink pods ~140.9 minutes ago to ensure no data gaps exist in the Iceberg table from that earlier disruption.
